text:
anika: Heads-up — during today's k6 replay I noticed a small cluster of requests to /v1/generate that returned 503 after ~700ms. Replay id: replay-2026-03-17-01. Only ~0.4% of traffic but consistent across two runs. Can perf/runtime look? I grabbed a few raw request/response snippets below.

mike: Thanks. Do you have the k6 config (vus/stages) and whether this was mirrored or direct replay?

anika: It was a mirrored replay (traffic-mirror-2026). k6 run used 500 vus, ramp to 500 over 5m, sustain 20m. Script is the usual replay runner (I attached the minimal snippet). The failures all hit the same host hostname=gpu-rt-12.

carmen: Can you paste the raw error snippet? Also was KV cache warm for those traces or cold starts?

anika: snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T01:12:34Z] curl POST /v1/generate -> 503 (UpstreamClosedError) latency=712ms host=gpu-rt-12 shard=2
[2026-03-17T01:12:34Z] backend: conn reset before headers
```
KV cache hit rate for this run ~82% (so not a full cold-start wave).

kai: Interesting. Could be a transient process restart or OOM that briefly closed sockets. Any OOM logs on gpu-rt-12 around that time in node-exporter or dmesg?

perf-bot: quick-check: ran p95/p99 probe against gpu-rt-12 for the window 01:10-01:15 UTC — p95=180ms, p99=690ms, 503 count=12 over 5m. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/probes/replay-2026-03-17-01

mike: That p99 aligns with your 700ms. If it's a process restart it could show as conn closed then immediate reconnects. Can we correlate with deploys / autoscale events? Any canary rollouts at that hour?

anika: No deploys scheduled. Autoscale logs show a tiny scale-up on the dedicated pool at 01:11 but nothing dramatic (added 1 pod). I can paste the autoscaler events if helpful.

carmen: I'll spin a focused locust run against gpu-rt-12 to try to reproduce with a ~1% blast of the same request pattern (long context lengths). Command I'll use:
```
locust -f locust_replay.py --headless -u 50 -r 5 --run-time 15m --host https://gpu-rt-12.internal
```
I'll start tonight at 02:00 UTC and monitor.

kai: When you run it, enable socket tracing on the host: sudo ss -tpanic -o state established '( sport = :443 )' and also tail the runtime logs with debug for connection pool: /var/log/redwood/runtime/debug.log.

mike: I'll add a quick log filter in observability to surface "UpstreamClosedError" + host=gpu-rt-12 and pin a small dashboard. Also adding a temporary alert if 5+ 503s in 10m.

anika: Perfect. Can someone from oncall watch the run? @sre-oncall?

sre-oncall: I can be on watch from 01:50-03:00 UTC. Will escalate if we see repeated 503s or host flapping.

perf-bot: pre-run checklist posted to run: https://perf.redwood/runs/1777777777-checklist
Checks: KV cache warm, no deploys, autoscaler readonly, perf probes active — all green except autoscaler flagged as minimal-change.

carmen: After my locust run I'll also capture tcpdump for any reset flags and upload pcap to S3.

mike: If locust reproduces, next step is bisecting kernel/container image and checking cgroups + oom events. If not reproducible under targeted load, it might be replay-specific (headers, client-side timeouts). Also check k6 request pacing — a microburst may expose a backend bug.

anika: OK — plan: carmen runs locust @02:00 UTC, mike sets dashboard/alert, kai collects socket+debug traces, sRE watches. We'll reconvene in this thread after run. Thanks folks :thumbsup:

carmen: noted — will post logs + pcap afterwards and a short summary. If I can't reproduce I'll try a mirrored run at scale (500 vus) but in a smaller window.

mike: FYI I added a small tracing span to the replay harness to capture request id + backend host mapping for the next replays, so we should have better correlation data going forward.

anika: awesome. Thanks everyone.
